LEVELS.name: Start
LEVELS.idea: Try one real task with one assistant.

LEVELS.name: Use
LEVELS.idea: Work with an agent daily and check it.

LEVELS.name: Shape
LEVELS.idea: Give it your context, standards and limits.

LEVELS.name: Scale
LEVELS.idea: Run agents in parallel and share your setup.

steps: Get access to one assistant and find out which data your client allows in it.
Give it one real task from today's work.
Ask it to explain something you do not understand.
Use it daily and let it ask you questions before it starts.
Read and correct its plan before it acts.
Check what comes out, and start a new session when answers get worse.
Connect it to the sources you work in.
Turn what you repeat into skills.
Limit what it can reach, and review at every handoff.
Run agents in parallel or on a schedule.
Choose what is worth doing, not what is possible.
Share your setup with the team.
tests: You have used it on real work five days in a row
You reach for it first, and you can explain everything you deliver
A colleague would get the same quality with your setup
Work gets done while you do something else, and others use what you built

steps: Install a coding agent in a repository you know.
Ask it to explain a part of the code.
Let it make one small change and read every line.
Work in plan mode.
Write issues the agent can solve from the text alone.
Push only what you can defend in review.
Put conventions and good examples into the codebase.
Spend time on domain and architecture tests instead of prompts.
Give the agent the backlog, repository and logs, inside a sandbox.
Run parallel sessions where one agent checks another.
Test the architecture itself.
Settle who owns code that no human wrote.
tests: You have merged one small agent-written change that you fully understand
An agent has made a change across several files that you reviewed and stand behind
A fresh agent session follows your conventions without being told
You steer several agents and still know why the code looks the way it does

steps: Take a real design question to the assistant.
Transcribe one interview and ask for patterns.
Compare the answer with your own notes.
Give the agent your Figma structure, not a screenshot.
Learn enough Git to open a pull request.
Use AI in each research step, and check each handoff.
Work on the handover from design to code.
Explore variants before you choose.
Tie what you make to the product strategy.
Start the day from pull requests and read design out of code with the agent's help.
Say no to nice-to-haves.
Share your research setup and write down the practice.
tests: You have checked one AI summary against your raw material
You have delivered one design change as a pull request
You tested several variants and can say why you chose one
You can review a change that arrives as code, and a colleague can use your setup

steps: Describe a real problem and let the assistant ask you questions.
Transcribe one meeting.
Let it draft something you would write anyway, then edit it.
Work in a Project per client or case.
Connect your files, email and spreadsheets.
Check every number against the source.

Reuse the same structured input for reports, templates and business cases.
Schedule tasks that prepare work before you need it.
Turn routines into skills and processes others can run.
Build in checks that catch errors before the client sees them.
tests: One AI-assisted draft has gone out in your name after your own edits
You describe problems to it instead of only asking for facts
A new deliverable starts from your material, not a blank page

steps: Team: say out loud that everyone is expected to try, and nobody is behind.
Organization: give access to tools.
Organization: publish which tools and data are allowed.
Team: agree on roles, definition of done and shared rules for AI use.
Team: no agent writes to production.
Organization: offer a planned way to learn, and a place to share.
Team: share project skills, write decisions down, test the codebase conventions.
Organization: set aside time for quality culture.
Organization: build a shared knowledge base, and local models where privacy needs them.
Team: rework the process for smaller teams.
Team: agree how people and agents share ownership.
Organization: build a software factory, one agreed way of building with agents, and name who owns it.
tests: Everyone on the team has access and knows the data rules
